title: Cruise Ship Pianist Rescued After Nine Hours in the Pacific
summary: Two fishermen off the coast of California spotted something surprising in the water about 20 miles from shore: a man, treading water, all alone in the Pacific Ocean. 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat,' Garrett recalled saying. The man told them he was a pianist on the Ovation of the Seas, a big cruise ship. He had been in the water for about nine hours. 'The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'' Norton said. The fishermen pulled him from the water and called for help. The Coast Guard and lifeguards took over, and confirmed he worked on the ship. Norton said the man was lucky in one big way: the ocean was unusually warm. The water was 76 degrees Fahrenheit. 'You have this crazy super El Niño year,' Norton said. 'A different year, no way he makes it.' How the pianist ended up in the water is not clear. Two fishermen in the right place at the right time, and a very warm ocean, helped save his life.
why_it_matters: If you ever go swimming in the sea, this story shows why warm water, luck and kind strangers can matter so much.
